# Exchange Online Hardening Kanban

Board updated: 2026-09-22 (generation 17; batch 20260922-aftermerge, three tests-first claims and three queued To Do reservations; 60 executable cards: 47 To Do, 3 In Progress, 10 Done; 13 non-counted summary parents).
Source: repository acceptance assessment and scope decision, 2026-09-19.

## Scope And Authority

- This is the authoritative status and force-rank index. [Backlog](backlog.md) holds acceptance criteria, dependencies, verification, and the disposition of every former active card.
- Deliver only Exchange Online configuration, mailbox operations, Exchange RBAC, email protection for Exchange recipients, Exchange-scoped governance, and the scripts, runbooks, evidence, and tests needed for that service.
- Tenant creation, subscription/license assignment, Entra identities/Conditional Access/PIM/consent, enterprise signing infrastructure, DNS/HTTPS hosting, tenant-wide Purview policy administration, SIEM onboarding, other M365 workloads, and vendor setup are outside this delivery backlog. Track their assumptions, risks, issues, and external dependencies in [RAID](RAID.md). Do not create other-party In Progress cards for them.
- EOP and licensed Defender email protection remain in scope only for Exchange recipients. Safe Documents, SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams configuration do not. Exchange mailbox hold/IRM settings may consume approved legal policy; designing legal policy or provisioning Purview is not Exchange work.
- Removing a tenant dependency from this board is not a claim that the dependency is satisfied. Report Exchange conformance and external readiness separately; never relabel unknown external state as a verified Pass.
- EXR-002/003/005/006/007/008/009 retain Done for their bounded offline acceptance. EXR-001 is reclosed on boundary checks and full-regression reconciliation; EXR-011-A01 (g13) and EXR-010-A01 (g16) are closed on scoped acceptance, affected regression reconciliation and independent review; EXR-004 remains reopened. EXR-007 completes inventory and proposal admission, not implementation of all recommendations. No current full-suite, live-service or release acceptance is claimed; external readiness remains unconfirmed.

## Execution Rules

- Force rank is unique and binding: select the lowest-numbered eligible card. Dependencies must be Done with evidence; no fan-out heuristic may override this explicit user ranking.
- Standalone WIP limit: one implementation card. Explicitly started Cohorts use one implementation card per cohort under the [cohort protocol](cohorts.md). Generation 17 retains Purple/Kanban as sole writer under serialized root, with one active and one queued card per cohort in batch2. Only three named Coworker-1 test files are writable; Coworker-2 implementation pending, Common unassigned/read-only, Coworker-3 read-only. Exact agents available at root, nested Cohort unavailable; no role spawns. ALL phases/commands serialize with fresh worker-reported TEMP GUID/output per invocation. Reports target 120 seconds while host permits; disclose synchronous delays. No autonomous background work, scheduled messages, hidden process or live operation is running or promised.
- Named Coworker invocation succeeded for the EXR-008 completion pass after earlier registration failures. Any fallback must retain the same single-worker limit, scope, ownership, review and no-tenant-operation constraints.
- Missing external prerequisites remain in RAID with an accountable role and verification condition. Leave affected Exchange work To Do and select the next eligible rank; do not invent a Blocked bucket or assign tenant work to the swarm.
- Every card uses negative-first Arrange-Act-Assert checks and one positive per behavioral unit. Add assertions within the card, including documentation and design cards.
- Done requires recorded passing verification and acceptance evidence. A green synthetic fixture is not live compatibility proof. Live validation needs explicit authorization and an independently supplied disposable environment.
- Preserve unrelated worktree changes. No blanket deletion of legacy tests or weakening of change safety to achieve a green run.
